section: Revolt of 1857 - economic, socio-religious, administrative and military causes
subsections: Earlier sepoy mutinies - causes and dates

accepted.s: Which one of the following mutinies took place in July 1806?
o: Barrackpore mutiny of the 34th Native Infantry
Barrackpore mutiny of the 47th Native Infantry
accepted.x: The Vellore mutiny took place in July 1806. It was associated with the controversial military dress regulations and religious apprehensions.
accepted.tq: Use the direct date–event association.
accepted.sec: Earlier sepoy mutinies - causes and dates  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Vellore mutiny of 1806 was chiefly triggered by which of the following measures?
o: Introduction of a new dress code and prohibition of caste marks and earrings
Refusal to cross the sea to Burma
Refusal to use the new rifle cartridges
accepted.x: The new dress code, including a turban with a leather cockade and restrictions on caste marks and earrings, caused resentment among the sepoys at Vellore.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the cause attached to a specific mutiny.
accepted.sec: Earlier sepoy mutinies - causes and dates  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Barrackpore mutiny of November 1824 was caused by the sepoys’ refusal to—
accepted.x: The 47th Native Infantry at Barrackpore refused to go to Burma by sea during the First Anglo-Burmese War.
accepted.tq: Apply the who–cause–event linkage.
accepted.sec: Earlier sepoy mutinies - causes and dates  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
a. Vellore mutiny — July 1806
b. Barrackpore mutiny of the 47th Native Infantry — November 1824
c. Berhampur mutiny of the 19th Native Infantry — February 1857
d. Barrackpore mutiny of the 34th Native Infantry — 29 March 1857
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Berhampur involved refusal of the new cartridges, while Mangal Pandey’s attack at Barrackpore occurred on 29 March 1857.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure date–event pairs and eliminate mismatched combinations.
accepted.sec: Earlier sepoy mutinies - causes and dates  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: 38th Native Infantry — Refusal to go to Burma in 1852
19th Native Infantry — Attack on officers at Barrackpore on 29 March 1857
accepted.x: The attack at Barrackpore on 29 March 1857 was carried out by Mangal Pandey of the 34th Native Infantry. The 19th Native Infantry at Berhampur refused the new cartridges in February 1857.
accepted.tq: Find the wrong person–regiment association.
accepted.sec: Earlier sepoy mutinies - causes and dates  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Santhal revolt of 1855–56 is distinguished from the mutinies listed in the context of the 1857 uprising because it was—
o: the first mutiny of the 34th Native Infantry
a civil revolt rather than a sepoy revolt
an uprising caused by the new cartridges
a military revolt over sea service
accepted.x: The Santhal revolt of 1855–56 was a civil revolt and not a sepoy mutiny.
accepted.tq: Separate a civil revolt from a military mutiny.
accepted.sec: Earlier sepoy mutinies - causes and dates  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Barrackpore mutiny of the 47th Native Infantry
B. Vellore mutiny
C. Berhampur refusal of the new cartridges
D. Mangal Pandey’s attack at Barrackpore
accepted.x: The correct sequence is Vellore mutiny in July 1806, Barrackpore mutiny in November 1824, Berhampur in February 1857 and Mangal Pandey’s attack on 29 March 1857.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the intervening events.
accepted.sec: Earlier sepoy mutinies - causes and dates  [other exams]

accepted.s: Mangal Pandey was hanged and his regiment was disbanded on—
accepted.x: Mangal Pandey was hanged and the regiment was disbanded on 8 April 1857. His attack had taken place earlier, on 29 March 1857.
accepted.tq: Distinguish closely spaced dates in a sequence of events.
accepted.sec: Earlier sepoy mutinies - causes and dates  [other exams]

accepted.s: What immediately preceded the Meerut rising of 10 May 1857?
o: The proclamation of Bahadur Shah II as Shahenshah-e-Hindustan
The sentencing of 85 sepoys of the 3rd Native Cavalry to ten years’ imprisonment
The disbandment of Mangal Pandey’s regiment
The refusal of the 19th Native Infantry to use the rifle
accepted.x: On 9 May 1857, 85 sepoys of the 3rd Native Cavalry at Meerut were sentenced to ten years. The rising followed on 10 May, when officers were shot and imprisoned comrades were freed.
accepted.tq: Identify the immediately preceding event rather than the later consequence.
accepted.sec: Earlier sepoy mutinies - causes and dates  [other exams]

accepted.s: The rebels who reached Delhi on 11–12 May 1857 proclaimed whom as Shahenshah-e-Hindustan?
accepted.x: After reaching Delhi, the rebels proclaimed Bahadur Shah II as Shahenshah-e-Hindustan on 11–12 May 1857.
accepted.tq: Match the political title with the associated leader.
accepted.sec: Earlier sepoy mutinies - causes and dates  [other exams]

accepted.s: The abolition of Sati in 1829 was resented by orthodox sections primarily because it was viewed as—
o: an attempt to abolish temple taxation
accepted.x: The abolition of Sati was perceived by orthodox groups as interference in established custom.
accepted.tq: Link a social law with the specific form of resentment it generated.
accepted.sec: Socio-religious causes - social laws, missionaries  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which British Governor-General is associated with the abolition of Sati in 1829?
accepted.x: The abolition of Sati in 1829 was carried out during the tenure of Lord William Bentinck.
accepted.tq: Use the reformer–reform association while avoiding ruler-swapping traps.
accepted.sec: Socio-religious causes - social laws, missionaries  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Lex Loci Act, also known as the Religious or Caste Disabilities Act, was enacted in—
accepted.x: The Religious Disabilities Act, also called the Caste Disabilities Removal Act or Lex Loci Act, was enacted in 1850.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between closely related reform dates.
accepted.sec: Socio-religious causes - social laws, missionaries  [other exams]

accepted.s: What provision of the Religious Disabilities Act of 1850 particularly alarmed orthodox sections?
o: It prohibited the taxation of religious lands
It abolished the zamindari system throughout India
It permitted converts to Christianity to inherit ancestral property
It granted sepoys exemption from overseas service
accepted.x: The Act enabled converts to Christianity to inherit ancestral property, which was viewed as an incentive for conversion.
accepted.tq: Identify the practical consequence behind a source of religious apprehension.
accepted.sec: Socio-religious causes - social laws, missionaries  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Christian missionaries preached under police protection.
2. Missionaries criticised Hindu and Islamic practices.
3. Western education, railways and the telegraph generated fears of mass conversion.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Missionary activity under official protection and the spread of Western institutions created apprehensions about religious conversion and the loss of caste identity.
accepted.tq: Test a cluster of related causes through an all-inclusive option.
accepted.sec: Socio-religious causes - social laws, missionaries  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT among the socio-religious apprehensions that contributed to discontent before 1857?
o: Complete withdrawal of missionary activity from British India
Social discrimination and racial arrogance of officials
Taxation of temple and mosque lands
Laws against child marriage and female infanticide
accepted.x: Missionaries operated under police protection; their activity was not completely withdrawn. Taxation of religious lands, social legislation, racial arrogance and discrimination contributed to resentment.
accepted.tq: Reject the absolute reversal of a stated condition.
accepted.sec: Socio-religious causes - social laws, missionaries  [other exams]

accepted.s: Under the Permanent, Ryotwari and Mahalwari systems, the principal economic burden on peasants was—
o: rigid collection of high land revenue
accepted.x: High land revenue was collected rigidly under the Permanent, Ryotwari and Mahalwari settlements, placing severe pressure on peasants.
accepted.tq: Identify the common feature shared by different revenue settlements.
accepted.sec: Economic causes - revenue settlements, taluqdars, Inam Commission, artisans

accepted.s: What was a major consequence of the high and rigid land revenue demand on peasants?
o: They became independent of moneylenders and traders
They were driven into debt and lost land to moneylenders and traders
They were exempted from commercial cultivation
accepted.x: The heavy revenue burden pushed peasants into debt, often resulting in the loss of their land to moneylenders and traders.
accepted.tq: Follow the economic cause to its immediate social consequence.
accepted.sec: Economic causes - revenue settlements, taluqdars, Inam Commission, artisans

accepted.s: Commercialisation of agriculture under British rule often compelled peasants to—
o: cultivate cash crops under high taxation
produce goods exclusively for princely courts
grow only food grains for local consumption
accepted.x: Commercialisation forced peasants to grow cash crops while they continued to face high land revenue demands.
accepted.tq: Apply the definition of commercialisation to the agrarian situation.
accepted.sec: Economic causes - revenue settlements, taluqdars, Inam Commission, artisans

accepted.s: The taluqdars of Awadh lost their estates under the—
accepted.x: The taluqdars of Awadh lost their estates under the summary settlement of 1856, making them strongly anti-British.
accepted.tq: Match the affected landed group with the correct administrative measure and year.
accepted.sec: Economic causes - revenue settlements, taluqdars, Inam Commission, artisans

accepted.s: The Inam Commission, established in Bombay in 1852, is associated with the confiscation of approximately—
accepted.x: The Inam Commission confiscated about 20,000 estates whose owners could not produce valid title deeds.
accepted.tq: Use the distinctive quantitative figure attached to an institution.
accepted.sec: Economic causes - revenue settlements, taluqdars, Inam Commission, artisans

accepted.s: Why did the actions of the Inam Commission create resentment among landholders?
o: It transferred all estates to Indian artisans
It confiscated estates when owners could not show title
It abolished all taxation on religious lands
It restored estates without examining ownership claims
accepted.x: The Commission confiscated estates whose owners were unable to establish legal title, thereby creating insecurity among landholders.
accepted.tq: Connect an institution’s procedure with its political consequence.
accepted.sec: Economic causes - revenue settlements, taluqdars, Inam Commission, artisans

accepted.s: Which of the following best explains the ruin of Indian artisans and handicrafts before 1857?
o: The Industrial Revolution reduced the supply of British textiles
Indian handicrafts received increased princely patronage after annexations
British machine-made goods entered duty-free, while Indian goods faced heavy tariffs
British goods were excluded from Indian markets
accepted.x: Cheap British machine-made goods entered India with favourable treatment, while Indian goods faced heavy tariffs, contributing to deindustrialisation.
accepted.tq: Compare unequal trade treatment rather than focusing on only one factor.
accepted.sec: Economic causes - revenue settlements, taluqdars, Inam Commission, artisans

accepted.s:
The decline of traditional artisans was aggravated by which combination of factors?
1. Cheap British machine-made goods, especially textiles
2. Loss of princely court patronage after annexations
3. Increased demand for indigenous handicrafts by annexed courts
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Annexations ended princely patronage, while British machine-made goods, particularly textiles, damaged Indian handicrafts; statement 3 reverses this effect.
accepted.tq: Find the statement that reverses the stated economic trend.
accepted.sec: Economic causes - revenue settlements, taluqdars, Inam Commission, artisans

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Indian artisans — Deindustrialisation due to machine-made imports
Taluqdars of Awadh — Loss of estates under the 1856 summary settlement
Absentee sovereignty — Expansion of princely court patronage
accepted.x: Absentee sovereignty was associated with the drain of wealth to Britain, not with the expansion of princely court patronage. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
accepted.tq: Detect the reversed economic relationship in the final pair.
accepted.sec: Economic causes - revenue settlements, taluqdars, Inam Commission, artisans

accepted.s: The terms ‘absentee sovereignty’ and ‘drain of wealth’ in the context of the causes of 1857 refer primarily to—
o: the movement of peasants from villages to princely courts
the transfer of religious authority from temples to courts
the transfer of economic resources from India to Britain
the migration of British officials to Indian villages
accepted.x: Absentee sovereignty involved the extraction and transfer of wealth from India to Britain, contributing to economic resentment.
accepted.tq: Distinguish an economic concept from unrelated administrative or religious processes.
accepted.sec: Economic causes - revenue settlements, taluqdars, Inam Commission, artisans

accepted.s: Which of the following was an administrative cause of resentment before the Revolt of 1857?
o: Exclusion of Indians from high civil and military posts
Rapid and inexpensive justice for all social groups
Abolition of corruption in lower courts
Admission of Indians to all high civil and military posts
accepted.x: Indians were excluded from high civil and military posts, producing resentment against the colonial administrative structure.
accepted.tq: Identify the discriminatory administrative practice.
accepted.sec: Administrative causes - exclusion from high posts, corrupt courts and police

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the lower courts and police before 1857:
1. Corruption was rampant.
2. Justice was slow and costly.
3. The system generally favoured the poor over the rich.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The judicial system was slow, costly and generally favoured the rich, making statement 3 incorrect.
accepted.tq: Use the reversed comparison trap in the third statement.
accepted.sec: Administrative causes - exclusion from high posts, corrupt courts and police

accepted.s: The annexation of princely states adversely affected the colonial administration because it—
o: ended the drain of wealth to Britain
created employment for thousands of court officials and soldiers
restored the authority of all displaced rulers
threw officials, retainers and soldiers of princely courts out of work
accepted.x: Annexations displaced thousands of officials, retainers and soldiers who had depended on princely courts for employment and patronage.
accepted.tq: Trace the administrative consequence of annexation.
accepted.sec: Administrative causes - exclusion from high posts, corrupt courts and police

accepted.s: Which one of the following most accurately describes the character of British administration that contributed to discontent before 1857?
o: Administration based on complete equality in high posts
Inefficient and prejudiced administration with corruption in police and lower courts
Administration controlled entirely by Indian officials
accepted.x: The administration was inefficient and prejudiced; corruption was widespread in the police and lower courts, while Indians were excluded from high posts.
accepted.tq: Select the precise composite description rather than an absolute claim.
accepted.sec: Administrative causes - exclusion from high posts, corrupt courts and police
